subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: An agency is planning a large procurement but does not yet know what technological solutions exist in the market. Before deciding whether to use an IFB or RFP, the buyer should issue a(n):
questions.explain: An RFI is used to gather market intelligence and understand available solutions, best practices, and industry standards before drafting a formal solicitation.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: Which of the following is true regarding a Request for Information (RFI)?
options: An agency can directly award a contract to the best response from an RFI
An RFI is legally binding on the vendor who responds
An RFI is strictly a research and planning tool and cannot result in an award
RFIs require a public bid opening
questions.explain: An RFI is a pre-solicitation market research tool. It does not contain final specifications and cannot be used to execute a contract or make an award.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: When deciding whether to use an IFB or an RFP, what is the most important question a procurement officer should ask?
options: How quickly does the end-user need the item?
Is price the only consideration, or do we need to evaluate different vendor solutions and methodologies?
Is the budget above or below $1,000,000?
Does the vendor have a local office?
questions.explain: The defining factor between an IFB and RFP is whether the agency knows exactly what it wants and only needs a price (IFB), or if it needs to evaluate subjective factors like methodology or design (RFP).
